rules.name: Majority settles a claim
rules.statement: A claim is settled only when most reviewers gave the same answer. A split with no majority stays unsettled.
rules.risk: A tie credited to one side turns an open disagreement into a fact the map presents as checked.

sites.why: calls a claim confirmed only when more than half the votes on it say so
calls a claim disproved only when more than half the votes on it say so
sends a split with no majority to the unsettled outcome instead of crediting either side

rules.name: Three answers, nothing else
rules.statement: A reviewer answers holds up, disproved, or cannot tell. Any other word is refused rather than counted.
rules.risk: An unrecognised word quietly folded into a bucket credits an outcome nobody voted for.

sites.why: refuses to build the honesty record when a vote carries a word outside the three
fails the early check on the vote files for the same unknown word, while the reviewer is still nearby
tells every reviewer to answer cannot tell when the code settles nothing, so the third answer stays reachable

rules.name: Vote makes a challenge
rules.statement: A claim counts as challenged only when a reviewer voted on it.
rules.risk: Counting a claim as checked because it was handed out inflates how verified the map looks.

sites.why: counts the challenged claims as the captured list minus every claim that drew no vote
defines the challenged number as how many claims got a verdict, not how many were sent out

rules.name: Stopping early must be declared
rules.statement: A pass that leaves claims unvoted is refused unless someone declares that stopping early was deliberate. The declaration must say which claims were prioritized.
rules.risk: An undeclared gap reads as a finished check, so nobody learns that a thousand claims went unread.

sites.why: refuses the honesty record when a captured claim has no vote and nobody declared the stop
refuses a declared partial pass that does not say what it prioritized
states the refusal, because a planned stop and a dead batch of reviewers look identical from inside the tool
requires the written reason, because the counts say how many claims were checked and never why those ones

rules.name: Full surface stays in the record
rules.statement: A pass that checked only part of the map still records the size of the whole claim surface.
rules.risk: Recording the smaller number lets a pass over a fifth of the map ship looking complete.

sites.why: sets the total from the whole captured list, whatever share of it drew votes
forbids cutting the captured list down to what was checked as a way past the refusal

rules.name: Judged against the list reviewers saw
rules.statement: A vote about a claim missing from the list captured for the reviewers is refused.
rules.risk: A record built against a later snapshot describes a check that never happened on the map being shipped.

sites.why: refuses the record when a vote names a claim the captured list never held
requires capturing the list before any correction lands, so the two sides still describe one moment

rules.name: Disproved claim may not ship
rules.statement: A build stops when the map still carries a claim its reviewers disproved, word for word.
rules.risk: Reducing a whole pass to counts hides a wrong claim, because a correction and an ignored refutation look the same.

sites.why: fails the check when a disproved claim still matches a row of the finished map
turns each surviving disproved claim into a blocking finding of the closing report

rules.name: Cited but never opened
rules.statement: A file cited as evidence that the reviewer's own record never names fails the check. A file it only saw printed by a search is flagged, not failed.
rules.risk: A check that fails honest reading teaches the next reviewer to hide how it read.

sites.why: fails the check for a cited file that appears nowhere in the reviewer's own turn record
reports a file the reviewer only saw printed as worth a second look, without failing it
